subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA clauses — limited use and forwarding exceptions
messages:
From: Julia Patel <julia.patel@acmeretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Retail Legal <privacy@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - clarification on CCPA limited-use / forwarding

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team asked me to reach out with a couple of clarifying questions around the DPA language we received. Two specific points:

1) Forwarding/limited-use: We need to confirm whether Redwood's DPA (and any US state privacy addendum) allows Acme to forward user data to law enforcement, fraud investigators, or downstream analytics vendors under a "limited-use" exception. If permitted, can you confirm whether Redwood requires prior notice, a subpoena/Court order, or any additional contractual safeguards?

2) Subprocessors & transfers: If Redwood engages subprocessor vendors for fraud detection, do you (a) notify customers before onboarding, (b) allow specific carve-outs for certain categories of Personal Information, and (c) support contractual flow-downs?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the items our privacy team flagged (Acme_Questions_CCPLIST.xlsx). Can you point us to the best place in your DPA that addresses these topics or confirm redline language you would accept for limited-use forwarding and law-enforcement exception?

We'd like to close this before the procurement review next week. Would a short call with your privacy lead help?

Thanks,
Julia Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Retail

Attachment: Acme_Questions_CCPLIST.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Julia Patel <julia.patel@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - clarification on CCPA limited-use / forwarding

Julia — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. Quick summary from our side:

- Redwood treats customers as "service providers" (CCPA/CPRA) / processor-equivalent in US state addenda unless the customer is acting like a controller for the specific use.
- Forwarding to third parties: Redwood does not operate as a controller for customer data; we will not use customer data for our own purposes. Forwarding from the customer’s environment (i.e., Acme initiating a forward) is outside the DPA scope. However, Redwood may process or share data with subprocessors strictly to provide the service (e.g., fraud detection, hosting, cloud logs).
- Law enforcement/compelled disclosures: Redwood will comply with lawful requests but, as a matter of practice and the DPA, we require customers to notify us where permissible and we commit to narrow disclosure only in response to a valid legal process (subpoena, court order). We are willing to add a clause that forwarding/disclosure to law enforcement is limited to requests supported by appropriate legal process and that Redwood will resist overbroad requests where allowable.

I've attached a one-page summary of our current DPA and a suggested redline for the limited-use forwarding language (Redwood_DPA_Summary_v1.pdf).

Proposed next step: Neha and Marcus are our privacy/legal ops leads — can they propose specific redline text for your counsel? I'd also be happy to schedule a 20–30 minute call this week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Summary_v1.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme - clarification on CCPA limited-use / forwarding

Karthik / Marcus — quick internal note on acceptable redline language and risk: 

(Sharing my suggestions below to feed back to Acme counsel — this is internal and not for customer circulation yet.)

Suggested redline (high level):
"Redwood shall process Personal Information received from Customer solely for the purposes of performing the Services and as otherwise authorized in writing by Customer. Redwood shall not disclose or transfer Personal Information except: (a) to subprocessors bound by equivalent contractual obligations; (b) to comply with a valid subpoena, court order, or other legal process requiring disclosure; or (c) where Customer has provided prior written authorization to forward information to a named third party for Customer's business purposes. In the event of compelled disclosure, Redwood shall provide Customer with prompt notice, unless prohibited by law, and shall limit the scope of disclosed data to the minimum necessary."

Notes / concerns:
- The "prior written authorization" bucket is important for Acme's downstream analytics vendors; we should limit "prior written" to an authorization that is reasonably specific (vendor name and purpose) so we don't accept blanket authorizations.
- For fraud investigations, consider an exceptions process: Acme can request an emergency disclosure (e.g., ongoing fraud investigation) and Redwood will evaluate and respond within specified SLA (e.g., 48 hours). For particularly sensitive categories, require either subpoena or an Escalation Team approval.
- Subprocessor notifications: recommend we commit to 30 days notice for new subprocessors for regulated categories, with an expedited 7-day notice for high-risk security vendors. That mirrors other enterprise customers.

If you both agree, I'll prepare a short redline that maps to our DPA sections and send it to Julia.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Julia Patel <julia.patel@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - clarification on CCPA limited-use / forwarding

Julia — thanks for the questions and for the spreadsheet. Per our internal alignment (copied Neha and Marcus), below is the concise position and suggested redline language you can share with Acme counsel: 

1) Limited-use / Forwarding: Redwood will process Customer data strictly to provide the Services. We can accept a limited-use forwarding carve-out where Customer (a) provides prior written authorization that names the downstream recipient and purpose, or (b) a lawful process compels disclosure. We propose the following redline to add to the addendum: 

"Redwood shall process Personal Information received from Customer solely to provide the Services and as otherwise authorized by Customer in writing. Redwood will disclose Personal Information only: (i) to subprocessors under a written contract requiring substantially similar data protection obligations; (ii) in response to a valid subpoena, court order, or other lawful compulsion, provided Redwood will (where legally permissible) notify Customer promptly and limit disclosures to the minimum necessary; or (iii) to a named third party where Customer has provided prior written authorization specifying the recipient and the permitted purpose."

2) Subprocessors & transfers: Redwood provides 30 days' notice for new subprocessors and will aim for an expedited 7-day notice for critical security/fraud vendors. We will flow-down DPA-equivalent obligations to subprocessors.

Attachments and references: I attached the one-page DPA summary and uploaded a suggested redline to the Drive for your counsel to review. Links and attachments: Redwood_DPA_Summary_v1.pdf, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExample

Next step: If that language looks acceptable, we can circulate a short redline for counter-signature (DocuSign link available: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABCDEF) or schedule a 20-minute call to walk through. Please let me know what your counsel prefers.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
